The extremal number for a linear $3$‑uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices that contains no (not necessarily induced) linear path of length $5$ is exactly the size of a maximal star, i.e. the maximum number of edges obtainable by fixing one vertex and pairing the remaining vertices arbitrarily.  Hence  

\[
\mathrm{ex}_L(n,P_5)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\Big\rfloor .
\]

In particular, when $11\mid n$ this value is $\displaystyle\frac{n-1}{2}$ if $n$ is odd (which occurs for $n\equiv 11\pmod{22}$) and $\displaystyle\frac{n}{2}-\frac12$ otherwise, which is always the integer $\big\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\big\rfloor$.

**Answer:** $\displaystyle\mathrm{ex}_L(n,P_5)=\Big\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\Big\rfloor\,$.   

ANSWER: $\displaystyle\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor$
